content:
jamie_ops: :rotating_light: Paging oncall — customers reporting 502/SSL handshake failures to API endpoints. Noticed spike starting ~08:14 UTC. Root cause looks like TLS handshakes failing at Cloudflare edge pops. Details: some client connections drop during ClientHello/SNI negotiation.
incident-bot: Incident created: HIGH - Edge TLS handshake failures affecting api.redwood.inference. Pager duty: @oncall_maya
oncall_maya: I'm on it. Thanks @jamie_ops. Can you paste a failing curl and a dig please?
jamie_ops: here's a failing curl from my laptop:
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.inference/v1/health
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* SSL connection error
curl: (35) error:14094438:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert internal error
```
jamie_ops: dig to edge
```
$ dig api.redwood.inference +short
104.21.34.55
172.67.45.88
```
jamie_ops: re-tested with `curl --resolve 'api.redwood.inference:443:104.21.34.55'` -> same handshake failure. 
ryan_platform: I'm seeing increased handshake failure rate in our telemetry (TLS alert 40/unexpected_message) across Cloudflare edge IPs in EU and US-east. Failures ~30-40% of requests since 08:12 UTC.
natalie_support: Customer-facing: multiple customers in EU reporting degraded API responses and 5xx. Raising status page draft now. Which endpoints affected? embeddings and generation (text) are both showing errors.
sre_lead_oliver: Quick check — Cloudflare dashboard shows elevated TLS handshake errors on multiple POPs. Also field 'unanticipated TLS backend response' for our origin seen in logs. @cloudflare-bot can you confirm if they're rolling anything? 
cloudflare-bot: Cloudflare status update: "Investigating: TLS handshake anomalies in multiple edge locations affecting SNI negotiation" - https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/ (monitoring)
oncall_maya: Ok. Mitigation plan: 1) Verify origin cert chain and SNI config 2) Try origin-pull bypass for a small % to test direct origin connections 3) Adjust routing policy to fallback pool for non-critical traffic 4) Notify support and customers. Who can flip a canary rule to bypass Cloudflare for 5% of traffic? 
ryan_platform: I can deploy a canary to route 5% of traffic through our direct load balancer (skip CF) — will create a temporary route and health-check. Doing it now. 
jamie_ops: I double-checked origin cert — valid, full chain present. No recent cert rotations.
sre_lead_oliver: Adding logs from the origin showing TLS incoming looks normal. The failure appears during Cloudflare->client SNI negotiation, not origin auth.
ryan_platform: Canary is up: `route rollouts/edge-bypass -> 5%` applied. Monitoring... 
```
# healthcheck
GET https://direct-api.redwood.inference/v1/health 200 OK
```
ryan_platform: Canary success: direct path shows 0% handshake failures so far. Cloudflare path still failing.
oncall_maya: Good. Next: escalate to Cloudflare support with packet capture and SNI trace. @jamie_ops can you grab a tcpdump of handshake from affected edge ip? Use `openssl s_client -connect 104.21.34.55:443 -servername api.redwood.inference -msg -state` and attach output.
jamie_ops: attaching output below (snip):
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
>>> TLS 1.3, Handshake, ClientHello
... 
SSL3 alert write:warning:shutdown while in init
```
jamie_ops: Uploaded tcpdump to the incident thread (link: https://internal.storage/incident/1999543210/tcpdump.pcap)
incident-bot: Pager duty: acknowledged by @oncall_maya. Severity -> Sev2. Time open: 12m
natalie_support: Draft status page: "We are investigating an issue impacting API connectivity for a subset of customers in EU and US-east. Some requests may fail with TLS or 5xx errors. We're working with our edge provider to mitigate."
oncall_maya: Escalation: opened Cloudflare ticket 123456 - provided pcap and s_client logs. Also asked CF to check for recent edge kernel/worker changes and SNI routing anomalies.
cloudflare-bot: Cloudflare reply: "Confirmed anomalies on a subset of edge nodes due to an internal routing config push. Engineering rolling a fix to affected POPs. Estimated mitigation in 20-40 minutes." 
ryan_platform: Rolling increase of bypass route to 20% to reduce customer impact while CF remediates. Monitoring metrics: errors dropping from 38% -> 12% in last 3m.
jamie_ops: Support: please prioritize top-tier customers with known SLA requirements — share the bypass endpoint and temporary instructions to us.
natalie_support: Noted. Sending targeted messages now.
sre_lead_oliver: Note for postmortem: need to evaluate fallback routing automation and quicker circuit-breaker to route traffic away from provider-side config errors.
oncall_maya: Once Cloudflare reports fixed, we'll do a controlled ramp down of bypass. Temporary mitigation checklist appended:
```
- Canary bypass to direct LB (iptables NAT)
- Increase DNS TTLs? NO, keep low for rollback
- Update routing policy: route.noncritical -> bypass pool
- Notify customers via status page
- Keep pcap and logs for support ticket
```
jamie_ops: Cloudflare just updated: "Fix deployed to affected POPs — monitoring for stability." 
incident-bot: Incident update: Cloudflare reports fix deployed. Please monitor for 30 minutes before declaring resolved.
ryan_platform: Errors back to baseline ~1-2%. Direct bypass ramping back to 5%.
oncall_maya: Let's wait full 30m. If no regressions, declare resolved and start RCA. @sre_lead_oliver can you own the postmortem? 
sre_lead_oliver: Will own. Will include timeline, customer impact, decision log for bypass, and action items for automation.
jamie_ops: Thanks everyone. Closing notes: total impacted requests ~120k, peak error rate 42%, primary impact window 08:12-08:44 UTC. Customer outreach in progress.
incident-bot: Incident resolved after monitoring period. Severity downgraded. Created postmortem ticket PM-2026-042 in Jira.
